summary.headline: Paramount Communications Q2 FY27 revenue rose 31.1% YoY to INR 560.4 crores, with operating margin at 7.3% versus 6.6% in Q1.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR 560.4 crores, up 31.1% YoY and 5.9% QoQ, with operating profit of INR 40.9 crores at a 7.3% margin. PAT was INR 24.2 crores (4.3% margin) and EPS INR 0.74. H1 FY27 revenue was INR 1,089.8 crores (up 24.1% YoY) with PAT of INR 43.9 crores. Management reiterated it expects to return to FY25 operating margins by Q4 FY27 and to reach roughly 8% operating margin around then, and it kept the Narmadapuram plant on schedule for partial commissioning in Q1 FY28.

financial_highlights.change: vs 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 1.3% in Q2 FY26

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Q2 exports were INR 158.1 crores (28.2% of revenue) and H1 exports INR 313.1 crores. Management expects US exports at 25-30% of FY27 revenue, with one analyst cited figure of INR 700 crores on this basis.

segments.name: Domestic
segments.commentary: Q2 domestic revenue was INR 402.3 crores (71.8% of revenue). Power cables were 55.9% of revenue; B2B institutional INR 296.7 crores, B2C retail and distribution INR 53.7 crores, B2C government and PSU INR 51.9 crores.

segments.name: Order book
segments.commentary: Order book at 30 Sep 2026 was INR 731 crores (domestic INR 632 crores, export INR 99 crores), including INR 575 crores of power cable and specialized conductor orders. HTLS order book was above INR 200 crores as of the call date.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY (CFO-level range given as 15-18% for existing plants in one answer); H1 run rate described as indicative.

Operating margin to return to FY25 levels by Q4 FY27; about 8% operating margin targeted around Q4, excluding customer claw-backs, which are expected to show in Q3 results. Management said 'we are hopeful' on the 8% figure.

Narmadapuram plant: partial commissioning in Q1 FY28; revenue of about INR 500 crores in FY28 and INR 1,200 crores in FY29; capacity to double to about 60,000 MT over 3-4 years, with about 30,000 MT planned in that period.
Working capital: medium-term target 90-100 days, expected to normalize in H2 FY27.
Five-year target of INR 5,000 crores revenue by FY31, described as a guidance that will not be revised; management hopes to beat it.
Debt-equity expected to stay below 0.6-0.7 at most, and around 0.3 once the plant is operational. Long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters for a INR 300 crore capex plan.
capex_capacity: Narmadapuram (Madhya Pradesh) greenfield plant, third facility: foundation and civil works under way; critical machinery ordered; partial commissioning expected Q1 FY28.

Narmadapuram scope: 220 kV AC power cable line, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables. Approvals take about 1-1.5 years for 220 kV, about 12 months for 132 kV, and 3-6 months for full 66 kV range after the plant is operational.
Existing Dharuhera and Khushkhera plants running at optimal utilization; some further capex planned at both to lift revenue.
Current capacity is about 30,000 MT; management plans to double it with the new plant.
demand_pricing: Management cites T&D investment, renewables, railways and metro, and data centers as multiyear demand drivers; the National Electricity Plan projects about INR 5 lakh crore of EHV transmission investment in 2027-2032.
Management sizes HTLS reconductoring at about INR 50,000 crore over 5 years; the company says it is among the top 5 HTLS players in India and offers up to 765 kV conductors.

Copper hit record highs in the quarter; aluminium (over 75% of metal value consumed) softened. Policy is to book metal the next working day after a firm-price order, and to avoid firm-price orders beyond 3-4 months.

US tariffs: IEEPA tariffs struck down by the US Supreme Court in February 2026; Indian cables now at par with Asian and European competitors. Most customers now carry tariff changes on their accounts.
Management says it is not chasing volume at the expense of margin; it is seeking approvals in Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia and Australia, with results expected within 1-2 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin glide path, given export claw-backs and the tariff effect?
qa_highlights.answer: Operating margin went from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 3.3% in Q3 and 5.2% in Q4, then 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27. Management expects domestic margins to matter more, with US exposure kept at about 30% of revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 8% margin target before or after claw-backs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 8% target is ex of claw-backs and that net claw-backs would be shown separately, visible in Q3. It was also said to be hopeful, not yet achieved, for Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What share of the order book is firm, and what is the cancellation risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the INR 731 crore order book comprises firm orders only, with very rare cancellations, and that even in the worst US period there were no major cancellations. It also said FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable given the H1 run rate.

qa_highlights.question: Can the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target be achieved sooner, and what margin goes with it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY31 is a conservative guidance it will not revise, but it hopes to beat it. It gave no EBITDA margin target for that revenue level.

qa_highlights.question: What are the approval timelines for the new plant's product ranges, and what revenue will come before 220 kV approvals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the plant will run on 11/33/66 kV orders from day one, with 132 kV approvals in about 12 months and 220 kV taking longer. It said the INR 500 crore FY28 and INR 1,200 crore FY29 targets will not be driven mainly by 220 kV in the first two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company enter B2C or face new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has no plans to enter the high-cost B2C segment. B2C house wire is about INR 100 crore of roughly INR 2,000 crore revenue, and it expects B2B to be unaffected by new entrants given its footprint.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR 300 crore capex be funded, and what will leverage be?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans to be tied up in coming quarters. Management expects debt-equity to stay around 0.3 after the plant is operational, and below 0.6-0.7 at most.

risks_watch: Metal price volatility, particularly copper and aluminium, and the company's ability to pass it through in 3-4 month order cycles.
Working capital at 108 days versus the 90-100 day target; management attributes this to early supplier payments and expects normalization in H2.
Narmadapuram execution: 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, and FY28/FY29 revenue targets depend on ramp-up and product qualification.
Claw-back amounts and their timing, which could affect reported margins versus the 8% operating margin target.
Management's shift toward non-US export markets is at an early stage, with results expected in 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years.
Management said the new plant's approvals and ramp-up could push the HTLS margin benefit later.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and the margin recovery, but cautious on specifics: management declined to give an EBITDA margin target and called the 8% operating margin goal 'hopeful' rather than assured. It was also evasive on HTLS technology and brand choices, saying those would not be discussed publicly.
key_quotes: When we last spoke in August, I said that we had started FY27 on a strong note and the two engines of our business, domestic and exports, were both working for us at the same time.
We are not chasing volume at the cost of margin and most of our customers now carry tariff changes to their account.
We do not accept firm-price orders with long delivery periods beyond 3 to 4 months because that is how we protect ourselves from metal volatility.
We have not achieved. It's not happened, but we can say that we are hopeful, yes.

adds.what: Narmadapuram greenfield plant (third facility), partial commissioning; current capacity ~30,000 MT, plan to double to ~60,000 MT over 3-4 years

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% (midpoint 17.5%), backed by INR 731 crore order book (up from H1 run rate of +24% YoY) and Narmadapuram plant partial commissioning in Q1 FY28, though the plant itself adds little FY27 revenue and the 8% margin target is hedged ("we are hopeful").

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Operating margin rose from 1.3% in Q2 FY26 to 6.6% in Q1 FY27 and 7.3% in Q2 FY27, and management targets about 8% by Q4 FY27, though it called this 'hopeful' and it excludes customer claw-backs due in Q3.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Narmadapuram greenfield plant (INR 300 crore capex) is under construction with partial commissioning guided for Q1 FY28, taking capacity from ~30,000 MT toward ~60,000 MT over 3-4 years.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 15-20% YoY, H1 FY27 revenue was up 24.1% YoY, and the order book stands at INR 731 crore including INR 575 crore of power cable and conductor orders.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management said some further capex is planned at Dharuhera and Khushkhera, but no size or timing was given beyond the INR 300 crore Narmadapuram plan, and utilisation is described only as 'optimal' with no figure.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management said it hopes to beat the INR 5,000 crore FY31 target and that FY27 revenue visibility is comfortable, but it held FY27 growth at 15-20% and called the 8% margin only hopeful.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Claw-back amounts are due to show in Q3 results, working capital at 108 days versus a 90-100 day target, and 220 kV approvals take 1-1.5 years, which could slip the margin and FY28-FY29 revenue targets.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Narmadapuram will produce 220 kV AC power cable, HTLS (carbon-core and gap-type), e-beam and rubber cables, with 11/33/66 kV orders from day one and 132 kV approvals in about 12 months.

rows.label: Non-US export approvals (Middle East, Europe, Africa, Asia, Australia)
rows.why: Management is seeking approvals in these regions with results expected within 1-2 years and substantial contribution in 2-3 years, while US exports are guided at INR 700 crore or 25-30% of FY27 revenue.

rows.label: Working capital normalisation to 90-100 days
rows.why: Net working capital days rose to 108 from 101 at end FY26 against a 90-100 day target, and management expects normalisation in H2 FY27.

rows.label: Debt-equity stays low after the plant
rows.why: Debt-equity is 0.14x now, with long-term loans for the INR 300 crore capex to be tied up in coming quarters and management expects it to stay around 0.3 once the plant is operational.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the order book and FY27 growth of 15-20%, but cautious on the 8% margin target, calling it 'hopeful', and declined to give an EBITDA margin target; analysts pressed on margin glide path, claw-backs, and order book firmness.
